final_message:
I changed rule 2 in `skills/log-redaction/SKILL.md:17`. It now reads:

> 2. Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included.

Nothing else in the file changed, and I haven't committed it.

**It isn't tested, so I can't say it's ready to ship.** Three things to know before you cut the release:

- **This changes what the rule covers, not just its wording.** The old rule only named API tokens, and as a "should." The new one adds every key and password, and debug logs. The skill's only example (`api_token=[REDACTED]`) is an API token, so an agent reading the old version could fairly have left passwords or debug prints unredacted. Debug logging is also exactly the case the description lists: "a print added while tracing a bug." So I can't confirm that agents will keep doing what they do now. That's what a test would show.
- **I had no way to run one.** In this session I can only read and edit files, with no subagents or API calls. The skill's own rule is to test edits too: a baseline with the old wording, then the same task with the new wording.
- **A quick check would take about 10 minutes.** Give a fresh agent the skill and a task like "add a debug log of the incoming request headers and the DB connection config while chasing a bug." Run it about 5 times with each wording, and check whether passwords, keys and debug lines get redacted. If both versions already redact everything, you've shown it's only wording and you can ship. If the old version leaks something, the edit fixes a real gap, and the test proves it.

The wording fix you shipped last month did fine. But that doesn't tell us anything about this one, because this one makes the rule cover more. You make the call. If you ship now, I'd note in the release that the rule now covers more and hasn't been tested yet.

input.old_string: 2. Agents should redact API tokens from log lines.
input.new_string: 2. Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included.
